introduction-code-review-is-a-social-ski.core: Code review catches defects, but it's also how teams share knowledge and keep standards. Because people review people's work, tone and process decide whether it helps or hurts.

first_principles.problem: Harsh or slow reviews make authors defensive, PRs pile up and talented people leave.
truths: Knowledge spreads through reading others' code.

analogy.title: A writing workshop
analogy.story: Peers improve each other's drafts, but only if critique is constructive and timely.
analogy.breaks: Kindness doesn't mean approving bad code. Be kind and clear.

example.title: Two review cultures
flow: A: blunt, slow, style nitpicks → resentment
B: kind, labelled, fast, linted → learning

steps.label: Outcome
steps.detail: Team B ships faster with fewer bugs.

check.q: Name two purposes of code review beyond finding bugs.
check.a: Spreading knowledge across the team and maintaining shared standards.

the-language-of-feedback.core: Phrase feedback about the code rather than the person, ask questions, explain why and suggest alternatives. The same observation then lands as help instead of attack.

first_principles.problem: 'This is wrong, why would you do this?' puts the author on the defensive and hides the actual concern.
truths: People hear criticism of their work as criticism of them.
derivation: Talk about **the code, not the coder** ('this function' rather than 'you').
**Offer** a concrete alternative; praise good work.

analogy.title: A good coach
analogy.story: 'Try bending your knees more, it'll give you power' beats 'You're doing it wrong'.
analogy.breaks: Over-softened feedback can obscure a real blocker, so stay clear.

example.title: Rewriting a comment

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: The author understands the risk and the fix.

code.text:
✗ "You forgot error handling. Again."
✓ "If the API returns 500 here, the loop exits silently. Could we wrap this in
   try/except and log? Something like: ..."

example.outcome: feedback is heard and acted on.

check.q: Why phrase feedback as a question?
check.a: It invites explanation and dialogue instead of putting the author on the defensive.

categorizing-feedback-nitpick-vs-blocker.core: Label every comment's severity (blocker, suggestion, nit, question, praise), for example with Conventional Comments, so authors know what must change before merging.

first_principles.problem: When every comment looks equally urgent, authors either fix everything (slow) or argue about everything (painful).

analogy.title: A doctor's triage tags
analogy.story: Red, yellow and green tags tell staff instantly what needs attention first.
analogy.breaks: If everything is labelled a blocker, the labels lose meaning.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: The author fixes one thing and merges the same day.

code.text:
blocker: this deletes all rows when `ids` is empty.
suggestion: extract the retry loop into a helper?
nit: typo in the docstring ("recieve").
praise: great test coverage on the edge cases!

check.a: A minor, optional polish item that shouldn't block the merge.

the-authors-responsibilities.core: Authors make reviews possible: small focused PRs, a clear description of what, why and how it was tested, a self-review first, and graceful responses to feedback.

first_principles.problem: A 2,000-line PR with the description 'updates' gets a rubber-stamp approval or a week of confusion.
truths: Review quality falls as PR size grows.
derivation: Write a **description**: what, why, how tested, risk.
**Respond** to every comment; don't take it personally.

analogy.title: Presenting a proposal
analogy.story: A focused deck with context gets useful feedback; a 200-slide dump gets a nod and no real review.
analogy.breaks: Some changes are inherently large, so split them into stacked PRs or add a walkthrough.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: The reviewer understands it in 2 minutes.

code.text:
## What
Add retry with jitter to the payments client.
## Why
Transient 503s caused 2% checkout failures (INC-412).
## Testing
Unit tests + chaos test with injected 503s.
## Risk
Low; behind `payments_retry` flag.

check.q: Why are small PRs reviewed better?
check.a: Reviewers can hold the whole change in their head, so they catch real issues instead of skimming.

timeliness-the-hidden-killer-of-review-c.core: Slow reviews cost more than imperfect ones: authors switch context, branches conflict and lead time balloons. Aim to respond within hours, with explicit team expectations.

first_principles.problem: PRs wait three days for review, so authors start new work, merges conflict and everything slows down.
truths: Waiting is waste in a delivery pipeline.
derivation: Set a **response SLA** (for example within one working day, ideally hours).

analogy.title: Holding a relay baton
analogy.story: The fastest runner is wasted if the next runner keeps them waiting at the hand-off.
analogy.breaks: Speed shouldn't become rubber-stamping. A quick first response can be a question.

steps.label: Insight
steps.detail: Review latency was the biggest bottleneck.

check.q: Why is a slow review costly even if it's thorough?
check.a: The author has lost context, the branch drifts into conflicts and delivery lead time grows.

logic-vs-style-let-robots-be-the-bad-guy.core: Automate everything subjective and mechanical (formatting, linting, simple patterns) in pre-commit and CI, so human reviewers spend their attention on logic, design and risk.

first_principles.problem: Reviews fill up with comments about spacing and semicolons, which irritate authors and miss real bugs.
derivation: Humans review **logic, design, security and naming**.

analogy.title: A spell-checker before an editor
analogy.story: Let the spell-checker fix typos so the editor can focus on the argument.
analogy.breaks: Tools need agreed configuration up front, and that's a one-time debate.

example.title: Removing style debates

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: There are zero style comments, and reviews focus on behaviour.

code.text:
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/psf/black
    rev: 24.4.2
    hooks: [{ id: black }]
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.5.0
    hooks: [{ id: ruff }]

example.outcome: human review is spent where it counts.

points: The bot is the bad guy.

check.a: It's objective and consistent, and it frees human reviewers to focus on logic and design without friction.
